В деревне у Пронтеры у каждого мальчишки: In the village near Prontera every boy had a stick for a sword, but Alan had two: he carried the second one “for his squire.” No squire ever turned up, so Alan lugged both. First up the barn roof, first off the bridge into the river, first to get a whipping from his father's reins. His father grumbled, “Just once, be second.” His mother silently patched his trousers. Alan promised her that one day he'd bring home a knight's shield and hang it over the door for all the neighbors to see.
В первый день лагеря новичков Алан вызва: On the first day of the Novice camp, Alan challenged the instructor — a grey-haired Swordman with a broken nose. He lasted eight blows. On the ninth he was lying in the dust, laughing. The instructor offered him a hand: “Brave. Stupid. But brave.” Captain Garret watched from the gallery and said nothing. That evening Alan asked him when they hand out a knight's shield. “When you carry someone out of a fight besides yourself.” Alan decided the captain was joking. The captain wasn't.
Взбесившиеся поринги, роща — и Алан влет: Rabid Porings, a grove — and Alan charges in alone, because it's faster. The Willow didn't even blink. He came to on a root, with Vika bandaging his shoulder and insisting she wasn't the least bit afraid of blood. Her hands shook worse than his. Bran, meanwhile, was writing something. “Alan owes Vika one bandage,” he read aloud. Alan wanted to object, but his shoulder hurt. At the Jelly Gate, for the first time, he stopped on his own.
В Излуде испытание мечников — полоса из: The Swordman trial in Izlude is a course of posts over the sea: fall, and you start over, soaking wet, with the seniors laughing. Alan ran first and fell nine times, every time at full tilt. The best are chalked on the wall, and at the very top: “Iris: not once.” The guild master, one-eyed Rolf, shrugged: “She watched her feet. You watched the finish.” A girl with a two-hander on the pier said the same, only shorter: “Your feet.” The tenth time, Alan walked. He made it.
По традиции Излуда новый мечник дарит св: By Izlude tradition, a new Swordman gives his first wooden sword to the next Novice. Alan thought it over and gave away the second stick — the one “for his squire.” The boy grabbed it with both hands. That same day Rolf showed Alan his first real technique — a battle cry. Alan shouted at a Poring, and every Poring in the field came at him. “A cry is an invitation,” Rolf said while Alan fought them off. “Only call if you can handle the guests.” Alan handled them. Barely.
Испытаний у рыцарей Пронтеры несколько,: Prontera's knights have several trials, and Alan hated one in advance: an empty hall in the castle, a bench, and orders to wait until called. He counted the cracks in the floor. Twice he got up to leave. Twice he sat back down. They called him at dawn — out onto the parade ground, where the “wounded” lay beyond the line while the formation fell back. Alan didn't rush ahead. He carried out two and returned to the line. The examiner nodded: “A knight waits until his own are gathered. That's what the room was for.” For the first time, Alan didn't argue.
Бруно вышел во двор «Двух колоколов» с к: Bruno came out into the yard of the Two Bells with a poker: Alan was drilling forty steps back again. For a Lord Knight it's not enough to hold a blow — you have to lead the line away without leaving the wounded. A barrel lid for a shield, a sack of flour for a soldier. Bruno brought a second one: “Usually there are two wounded.” Alan reworked the whole drill. In the morning Greta presented a bill for the flour; Bran paid it and wrote down the debt. Alan didn't argue: learning is cheaper than losing your own.
В архиве Альдебарана прочли: «Вышли двое: In the Al De Baran archive they read: “Two came out: the captain and his squire.” Alan understood why Garret taught retreat, not victory speeches. At the evening debrief he demanded a headcount of the returned before splitting the loot. Then he wrote to the captain: “I get it. I think.” He never sent it; the letter stayed in his boot. He could already order a retreat. Telling his mentor that he now understood the cost of that order turned out to be harder.
В Гласт Хейме Алан узнал, кого вынес Гар: In Glast Heim, Alan learned whom Garret had carried out: the future Herald. “So retreating was for nothing?” The captain answered, “I carried out a man. What he did with his life was his choice. I'd carry him out again.” Alan sheathed his sword: no weapon could win this answer. Until dawn they dug graves for the knights. Alan worked alongside, not racing anyone; he handed his watch to Iris, because even a strong line holds only on its shifts.
После Нифльхейма Гаррет посвятил Алана у: After Niflheim, Garret knighted Alan at the north gate of Glast Heim. No trumpets, no crowd: just the wind and their own. Lord Knight training was no substitute for this recognition. The captain held out Prontera's old shield, nicked all over. Alan took it and stepped back, among the others: a shield belongs where the line needs it. Bran took out his notebook and wrote nothing. This time Alan didn't promise to be first. He took up his shift.
Орден Креста испытывает постом и ночью в: The Order of the Cross tests with fasting and a night on watch at the tombs of fallen brothers beneath Prontera's cathedral. Alan stood with a candle, reading the names on the slabs. It seemed to him they'd all stood up first. By morning he understood something else: behind each of them stood someone who lived. An old brother asked, “Whom will you cover with your shield?” “Everyone.” “Wrong. The one beside you. And there's always someone beside you.” The order gave Alan a heavy shield with a cross. He held it as if people already stood behind him.
В часовой башне шестерня сорвалась на Бр: In the Clock Tower a gear broke loose and fell toward Bran. Alan took the blow himself; by morning the bruise was his, and Bran's shoulder was fine. A Paladin's vow didn't make his body invulnerable. Alan had Bran check the fastenings while Vika bandaged him: a second hit like that could leave the line without a shield. The notebook gained a reverse entry: “Bran owes Alan one bruise.” Alan demanded interest. Bran refused — but checked every fastening.
«Вышли двое: капитан и оруженосец Ансгар: “Two came out: the captain and his squire Ansgar.” The chronicle named no one else. Alan asked the order to pray for Garret's company; the old brother asked for the names. A Paladin could take another's blow, but couldn't replace the fallen with a blank line. Three times Alan approached the captain and talked about the weather. The fourth time he heard: “Not now. When we get there.” He didn't push. The list waits in the cathedral; the right to tell it belongs to the one who came out.
На галерее Гласт Хейма Алан закрыл Вику: On the gallery of Glast Heim, Alan shielded Vika from the man in grey. She moved the shield aside: “The mark holds him. Not just his choice.” Alan gave her room but stayed within striking reach. That night by the graves he told Garret, “If it comes to it, I'll cover them both.” “You never did learn to retreat. Good.” The captain dictated the names of his company himself. Alan wrote each one down: a Paladin answers not only for those behind his shield right now.
После Нифльхейма Гаррет посвятил Алана у: After Niflheim, Garret knighted Alan at the north gate. The brothers of the order stood beside him; the Paladin chose a spot from which he could cover his neighbors, not the glamorous front rank. He took a day's leave, went home and hung the old shield with the cross over the door, as he'd promised his mother. His father asked, “First, then?” “In front of everyone.” His mother brought a sturdier nail. The new shield Alan left by the threshold: in the morning, back to his post.
Брану было двенадцать, когда пришли за ф: Bran was twelve when they came for the farm. The collector read the IOU aloud while the boy stood behind his mother and memorized the figures: forty-two silver, interest, penalties, “in the event of the borrower's death.” His mother died that same winter; the farm was taken in spring. Bran remembers the figures down to the last copper. Sometimes, when he can't sleep, he recounts them. It all adds up. That's exactly what's frightening.
Первую тетрадь Бран купил в лагере нович: Bran bought his first notebook at the Novice camp with a week's pay — instead of a new bowstring. The instructor said arrows matter more. Bran worked it out: a bow without arrows is exactly as useless as arrows without bookkeeping. On the first page he wrote: “Who owes how much.” The page stayed empty a long time — in camp everyone was equally poor. Then Alan arrived.
В первую неделю лагеря Бран заметил, что: In his first week at camp, Bran noticed the quartermaster charging Novices an extra copper for every bundle of arrows. He wrote it down, added it up and showed Garret the total: over a year it came to a new barracks roof. The quartermaster was sent to muck out the stables, and Garret leafed through the notebook and handed it back: “You count well. Now count those who came back from patrol.” Bran started a new column. It turned out to be the hardest: in it, nothing can be rounded.
Гильдия лучников в Пайоне испытывает про: The Archer guild in Payon tests simply: bring back shafts for arrows from the forest and don't break a single arrow on the way. Bran calculated everything — weight, steps, two trips — and got lost in the very first hollow. From behind a pine stepped a girl of about thirteen, the forester's daughter: “Don't cut the living. Deadwood's over there.” She led him, showed him and left without asking his name. Bran brought the shafts back exactly to count. A new entry appeared in the notebook: “Owe the girl from Payon: the way.” The first line in the column marked “me.”
Первый настоящий приём Брану показала ст: Bran's first real technique was shown to him by the guild's old master: two arrows into one target, almost without pause. “The first to hit. The second to make sure.” Bran thought and said, “The second is interest.” The master laughed for the first time that week. By Payon tradition, an Archer carves his name on his bow so the bow remembers its owner. Bran carved “Bran,” and below it, small, “42.” Forty-two silver. So the bow would remember not just its owner, but why he shoots.
В Хьюджеле охотников испытывают трижды:: In Hugel, Hunters are tested three times: track a beast by three trails, set a trap, and wait for a falcon — the falcon picks its master itself. Bran read the trails faster than anyone: trails are the same figures, just on the ground. The trap came out annoyingly neat. And the falcon landed not on his arm but on his open notebook, and pecked at the page marked “Alan.” Bran named it Percent: it takes its cut of every catch. Alan asked why not Bandage. Bran put that on his tab.
На затонувшем корабле Бран нанёс на карт: On the Sunken Ship, Bran mapped every horned mark. A Sniper reads not only the target but the path it's lured along. Fields, sewers, orcs, pyramids, Payon, the sea — one line leading north. Grey smoke drifted off after every victory. “We're not late. We're being led.” Bran recounted everything while Percent sat silent on his shoulder. Then he put away his arrow: before walking a trail, his comrades had to know who blazed it.
После Альдебарана Бран завёл страницу ка: After Al De Baran, Bran started a page for the captain: “Owes: a story. Due — when he decides.” Garret used to pay for everyone and leave before it was written down. Now Bran knew that not every debt can be collected on time. He showed him the page. “Fair,” said the captain. On patrol Bran took the far sector himself: while Garret gathers his answer, someone has to watch the road, not his past.
В соборе Гласт Хейма Бран сел переписыва: In the cathedral of Glast Heim, Bran sat down to copy out forty children's names. A Sniper was supposed to be looking for the next target; he asked Dorn to stand at the passage and not rush him. “They were lost and followed the dead. Someone has to remember them, not call them.” Last he wrote: “Til, son of Ansgar.” He checked every letter, closed the notebook and didn't look at Vika for a long time. Here, as in the column of those back from patrol, nothing could be rounded.
У цитадели Нифльхейма Бран вычеркнул дол: At the citadel of Niflheim, Bran crossed out Alan's debts: “In case we don't come back.” Then he checked his arrows and gave Percent a way back: another life shouldn't remain collateral for his accounts. They came back. At the Two Bells he restored every line from memory. “With interest.” Alan didn't argue. On the facing page remained names that are never crossed out. Bran knew how to tell these two kinds of entries apart.
Барды Комодо испытывают так: спой, чтобы: The bards of Comodo test like this: sing so the tavern goes quiet. Bran sang Alan's debts — in rhyme, with a chorus. The tavern roared. “A bard's first song is about those you love,” said the old bard. Bran was silent a long time, then sang the IOU: forty-two silver, interest, penalties, “in the event of the borrower's death.” No melody, almost a whisper. The tavern fell silent. Bran passed the trial and didn't pick up a lute for a week. The second song, about the debtor, he's still writing.
Когда Альдебаран забыл вчера, Бран сел н: When Al De Baran forgot yesterday, Bran sat on the town hall steps with his notebook. His Comodo Minstrel training let him hold a whole square with one voice; this time it was no act. A verse for each street: who was paid, who was wronged, who is awaited at home. He repeated the hard names until people recognized them. He sang to an old woman that she owed no one: he'd paid the baker himself. He put that in neither the notebook nor the song. Memory can't be returned with interest.
После строки «Вышли двое: капитан и оруж: After the line “Two came out: the captain and his squire Ansgar,” Bran wrote a ballad. Every verse ended with the two survivors. Garret listened: “Don't sing until you know who it's about.” Bran tore up the lyrics, though the melody already held the whole hall. A Minstrel's art could make people listen; it gave no right to speak for the dead. On a fresh page he wrote: “Owes: a story. Due — when he decides.” He left the melody waiting.
В соборе Гласт Хейма жрецы пели колыбель: In the cathedral of Glast Heim the priests sang a lullaby that called the living to the dead. Bran copied out the forty children's names and set them to another tune: not “come to me,” but “I remember you.” Instead of the usual chorus that quickens the battle step, he left each name room for a breath. Last came: “Til, son of Ansgar.” His voice wavered; Vika picked it up. Bran sang it to the end. This song couldn't be cut short for his own peace of mind.
У цитадели Нифльхейма Бран вычеркнул дол: At the citadel of Niflheim, Bran crossed out Alan's debts — in case they didn't come back. They came back. At the Two Bells he finally sang the second song, about the debtor: the whole list, from the bandage to the interest. This time he didn't hide behind a bow instead of a lute. Alan blushed at first, then sang loudest of all. Bran held the chorus so his tired comrades could sing along. For the first time, he believed it was art. Not out loud, of course.
Вику принесли к приюту собора Пронтеры в: Vika was brought to the orphanage of Prontera's cathedral in a bread basket. The one who brought her was a boy of about fifteen — skinny, in someone else's jacket — and he stayed on at the orphanage himself: mopped floors, hauled water, slept by the door of her room. Her brother. Father Benedict told how that first night the brother wouldn't let go of the basket and fell asleep sitting up. Vika herself remembers something else: a warm palm over a candle and a whisper, “Sleep, little flame.” That's how he put out her light every evening.
Когда Вике было одиннадцать, в Пронтеру: When Vika was eleven, a plague came to Prontera. Father Benedict went from bed to bed, and she carried water and bandages after him. Forty beds — forty little graves. Then Father Benedict vanished too. Ever since, Vika has been afraid of blood. Years later she was told the plague had taken her brother as well — they buried quickly, and she never got to say goodbye. Vika brings flowers to the grave with his name, because there's nowhere else to bring them.
В лагере новичков лекарь учил перевязкам: At the Novice camp, the medic taught bandaging on pig skin stretched over a barrel. Vika stitched fastest of all — neat, tiny, orphanage stitches. Then a real wounded man was brought into the infirmary, and she fainted right there, needle in hand. When she came to, the medic was stitching the wound himself and grumbling. “Again,” said Vika, and took the needle. Her hand shook, the seam came out crooked, but it held. Since then, before every bandaging she whispers, “It's just pig skin.” She doesn't believe it. She stitches.
Испытание собора Пронтеры — паломничеств: The trial of Prontera's cathedral is a pilgrimage to three hermits, on foot and without complaint. Vika feared not the road but the nights in the forest. With her went a boy just kicked out of the choir — Teo. He sang the whole way, and the wolves gave them a wide berth. Vika never told him she wasn't scared with him around. The first hermit asked why she wanted to serve. “So my hands stop shaking.” “If they shake, you feel. Go on.” She reached all three. Without complaint. Almost.
Первое исцеление у Вики вышло в приюте с: Vika's first Heal came in the cathedral orphanage, over a little boy who'd slashed his palm on a broken mug. Blood, screaming, hands trembling — and suddenly light flowed from under her fingers, steady and warm as a candle under a palm. Her hands shook. The light didn't. The boy stopped crying and stared at his palm, whole again. Vika went into the storeroom and cried there herself. The sister who taught the Acolytes later told her the cathedral's motto: “The light is not the one who shines, but the one who doesn't go out.” Vika remembered the second half.
Первое имя в списке: The First Name on the List
Испытание жрецов — ночь у изгнанных духо: The Priest trial is a night among banished spirits and a morning at a sickbed. Vika stood the night without giving ground: the spirits whispered in the voices of the orphanage, and she prayed until the whispering died. In the morning, at an old man's bedside, her hands didn't shake for the first time. A new Priest receives a biretta and the first name on the list of those they pray for. Vika wrote: “Father Benedict.” She was told one prays for the dead differently. “I don't know that he's dead,” Vika replied. No one argued.
После ночной перевязки Грета спросила, п: After a night bandaging, Greta asked why Vika snuffs candles with her palm. The High Priestess knew how to divide her strength among the wounded, but still guarded the story of her brother like a sore spot. He came every week, married by then, a son at home: an apple, a ribbon, “Sleep, little flame.” One week he didn't come. They said: the plague. Vika told it out loud for the first time. In the morning Greta set a candle in a glass by her bed. Now someone was looking after Vika too.
Архивариус Альдебарана прочёл: «Вышли дв: The archivist of Al De Baran read: “Two came out: the captain and his squire Ansgar.” “That was my brother's name. A common name… probably.” Vika went to bandage Dorn, who was perfectly fine. He let her check an old seam and asked no questions. The High Priestess knew worry isn't cured by one more prayer; still, she couldn't let go of his sleeve. Her brother had left as a squire too. That night she left the candle burning and asked Greta to sit with her.
Верховным жрецом Гласт Хейма оказался Бе: The High Priest of Glast Heim turned out to be Benedict. Vika fought her guardian without drawing her protection from the wounded, and forgave him. Before he died he confessed: her brother is alive — he is the Grey One. On the gallery a palm shielded a lantern; she knew the gesture before the face. “You've grown, little flame.” On her brother's hand was the horned mark. Vika asked the captain to hold the line: “The mark holds him. Not just his choice. We'll put this one out too.” Forgiveness didn't mean letting him through to her own.
Врата Нифльхейма закрывались только изну: The gates of Niflheim could only be closed from inside. Her brother stayed with the knights, beside his sleeping son; Vika let him go herself. The High Priestess didn't promise her comrades to heal what can't be healed. Once a week she comes to the north gate where Garret stands, sets down a candle and snuffs it with her palm: “Sleep, brother.” Then she returns to the wounded. Not because the grief has passed: the living still need her hands, and she needs the living.
В обители святой Капитолины испытывают н: At the cloister of Saint Capitolina, the test is a week of silence and a hundred blows to a sandbag. Silence, Vika could do. Striking — no. She'd spent her life bandaging, and here she had to hit. At the fortieth blow she started crying — forty beds in the plague — and didn't stop. At the hundredth she split her knuckles bloody and bandaged herself, with Father Benedict's knot. The abbot looked at the bandage, not the bag. “Now you shield, not just mend,” he said.
Вика хранит под бинтами письма: «Отец Бе: Under her bandages Vika keeps letters: “Father Benedict, I'm doing well.” Then — about the squad, Alan, Bran, Greta and Dorn's milk. There's nowhere to send them. Champion training taught her to hold back a blow and a breath, but gave her no address for her missing guardian. She writes once a week, the way her brother used to visit the orphanage. She doesn't reread them. Before her watch she folds the sheets neatly: her silence should keep what's unsaid, not keep her from hearing the wounded.
В Альдебаране прочли: «Вышли двое: капит: In Al De Baran they read: “Two came out: the captain and his squire Ansgar.” That was her brother's name. A common name. That evening Vika stood palm forward and held the stance until midnight. A Champion could stop a blade, but memory wouldn't stop: with this palm her brother snuffed the candle. Defense, not a strike. Greta left a candle in a glass on the windowsill. Vika unclenched her fingers: tomorrow they'd be shielding people again, not trying to hold on to one coincidence.
Против Бенедикта, Верховного жреца Гласт: Against Benedict, High Priest of Glast Heim, Vika went bare-handed. She took the blows, covering the wounded; she saved her Champion's counter for last and in the end never struck it. She forgave. He confessed: her brother is alive — he is the Grey One. On the gallery her brother shielded a lantern with his palm, but the mark was on his hand. Vika stayed between him and the squad. “The mark holds him. Not just his choice. We'll put this one out too.” Strong hands weren't meant for revenge on her guardian.
Брат остался закрыть врата Нифльхейма из: Her brother stayed to close the gates of Niflheim from inside, beside his sleeping son. Vika let him go, without trying to force him from his post. Once a week the Champion stands an hour at the north gate with Garret. In silence; this hour she gives to no one, and she doesn't blame herself for it. Then she sets down a candle and snuffs it with her palm: “Sleep, brother.” Before leaving she checks the captain's bandages. Someone in the squad is always wounded. Now she knows how to spare her own strength too.
Правил у бабушки было три. Старшую дочь: Grandma had three rules. The eldest daughter in the family is named Greta. The little bell over the door of the Two Bells is never to be taken down, sold or scoured with sand. People in grey hoods are not to be let into the house — not even in the rain, not even for double the price. Why, Grandma never explained: “Your great-great-grandfather said so.” Little Greta tested the first two rules and got her hands smacked. She never got around to testing the third.
Торговаться Грета начала в девять — с мо: Greta started haggling at nine — with the milkman who watered down the cream. At twelve she collected her first debt: a mercenary had been drinking on credit for three weeks, and Greta waited until he stood up, then slammed a frying pan on the table right next to his hand. Not on his hand — on the table. He paid, apologized and left a tip. Ever since, the frying pan has hung by the bar on its own nail. Bruno calls it “the bookkeeping.”
Серый капюшон сорвал колокольчик и ушёл: A grey hood snatched the little bell and fled into the forest. Greta grabbed her frying pan and ran after him — so fast she forgot to take off her apron. In the thicket Mastering swallowed her: three hours in pink jelly, beside the bell, in a darkness that smelled of strawberries. Greta pounded from inside, cursed and haggled with the jelly. When they pulled her out, the first thing she asked was where the bell was. The second — who was paying for the apron.
Гильдия торговцев в Альберте испытывает: The Merchant guild in Alberta tests like this: deliver a parcel halfway across the world and come back with a Kafra receipt. Greta rode on an Alberta carter's cart and within the first three miles haggled the fare down to zero: she promised to post his name on the board at the Two Bells. The carter haggled all the way to Morroc. The Kafra made the receipt out to both of them. Greta never did post the carter's name — she forgot to ask it. The guild's motto: “Everything has a price. Especially what's free.” Greta considers her ride honest.
Первому настоящему приёму торговцев учат: Merchants learn their first real technique in Alberta: the coin strike. You hit — and you pay, honestly, in ringing coin. Greta tried it once, calculated what a single fight would cost and went pale. “The frying pan is free,” she told the guild master. The master argued a long time. Greta haggled longer and ended up with a discount on her guild dues. She left the guild with a badge, a frying pan and three extra silver. Bruno still doesn't know where they came from.
Кузнецов в Эйнброхе испытывают так: выку: Blacksmiths in Einbroch are tested like this: forge a blade the senior master can't break. Greta forged a frying pan. The master beat it with a hammer, bent it, dropped it on the anvil — the pan rang and didn't bend. “This isn't a blade,” he said. “The edge is sharp,” said Greta. “Check.” The master didn't. Greta was handed the master's hammer amid general laughter. She hung the little bell on its handle, and now it rings before every blow. The master did stamp his mark on the frying pan after all.
Вернувшись с моря, Грета рассказала Брун: Back from the sea, Greta told Bruno about Helmut, the first Greta and the coffin on the seabed. The Mastersmith was used to answering for cracks in other people's weapons; a family loss can't be fixed with a hammer. For the first time her father didn't interrupt. He took out the bottle saved “for a wedding” and poured three mugs. The third he set out for Helmut and the girl. Greta didn't put it away when she wiped the bar. By morning the mug was empty. Bruno swears he didn't drink it. Greta believes him: not every farewell needs checking.
В архиве Альдебарана Грета нашла рецепт: In the Al De Baran archive, Greta found the recipe for the bell metal of Glast Heim's cathedral. It tells the dead “sleep” and “take the watch”; her little bell is a fragment of that changing of the guard. The Mastersmith refused to recast it for a cleaner ring: the alloy doesn't replace the oath. Bran raised her share by half a copper. That evening she carefully cleaned the metal, without sand. A tool the squad depends on can't be repaired on a hunch.
В соборе Гласт Хейма треснувший колокол: In the cathedral of Glast Heim, the cracked bell hummed without being struck. The little bell answered not like an echo — like family waiting on the doorstep. “Well, hello, Grandpa,” said Greta. Even Bran didn't laugh. She examined the crack and put away her hammer: a master's blow could shatter what still held memory. She asked Alan to cover the passage and listened to the ringing to the end. Not every damaged metal needs the strength of her hands.
В Нифльхейме Грета звонила смену караула: In Niflheim Greta rang the changing of the guard: “sleep” and “take the watch.” Her arm grew tired; she shifted her grip without breaking the ring. The dead lay down in rows; the Lord and the boy by the wall fell asleep. In Prontera they call her the Keeper of the Bell. Greta gets annoyed: the title doesn't excuse her from fixing the squad's weapons. The little bell hangs over the door of the Two Bells again and wakes the drunks. She didn't take it down even for a master's award. It has earned its rest.
Алхимики Альдебарана испытывают зельем б: The Alchemists of Al De Baran test with a potion made without a single mistake — and then you have to explain every drop. Greta explained in money: “This drop is three coppers. This one will save a hand, so it's priceless. This one we can skip — we'll save.” The examiners exchanged glances. The guild's motto is “precision is kindness,” and they took Greta for her head for figures. She kept the frying pan on her belt: in case the recipe didn't work. In the very first month, the recipe didn't work twice.
В трюме корабля Дрейка Грета узнала чёрн: In the hold of Drake's ship, Greta recognized the black bell before the name on the coffin: Helmut, her great-great-grandfather's brother. The Biochemist was used to checking the composition first. She scraped the residue into a vial: “salt, sea, a hundred years.” Then she set her tools aside and rang softly, the way Grandma did, saying goodbye. The vial stayed on her belt. She never did analyze it: she wouldn't turn a family farewell into an experiment. Some things the squad entrusts to her not for research.
Рецепт из Альдебарана Грета читала по пр: Greta read the recipe from Al De Baran by its proportions: copper, tin, silver, salt from a grave and the sign for “oath.” The Biochemist compared the ring against a sample: her little bell was made of that very cathedral metal. The alloy can be recreated; the promise can't. Bran added half a copper to her share. That evening Greta mixed a cleaner by the recipe, tested it on ordinary copper and only then touched the bell. A mistake here would cost more than all the loot.
Треснувший колокол Гласт Хейма загудел н: Glast Heim's cracked bell hummed to greet the little bell. But Vika could barely stand after fighting the man she had called father. Greta gave her the last vial and a handkerchief that smelled of onions. The Biochemist would have to go on without reserves; she told Alan in advance, so he wouldn't count on one more potion. In the ledger she wrote: “Not a loan.” Then she looked up at the bell: “Well, hello, Grandpa.” Even Bran didn't laugh.
В Нифльхейме Грета звонила смену караула: In Niflheim Greta rang the changing of the guard, and the dead lay down in rows. At home the Biochemist wrote up the bill for the expedition: vials, bandages, every drop. It came to a lot. She could have presented it to the cathedral, but stamped it with the guild seal and “paid.” Bruno asked, by whom. “By everyone who came back.” She hung the bill over the bar, and the bell over the door. She'll start gathering the next stock tomorrow. Today she won't make anyone pay for having survived.
В Морроке мальчишки дерутся за тень, вод: In Morroc, boys fight over shade, water and dates. Dorn was a head taller than everyone and fought for others: big fists, little anger. Once someone brought him a dead scorpion — to scare him. Dorn sat over it and cried: poor thing, it was so small. Zara remembers it to this day and brings it up at every opportunity. Dorn claims he got sand in his eye. In Morroc there's sand everywhere. Convenient.
Гильдия воров взяла Дорна под крыло в че: The Thieves' guild took Dorn under its wing at fourteen: fed him, taught him locks, gave him a roof. At eighteen Set presented the bill — for the roof, the food, the wing. Dorn hauled cargo, stood at doors, beat other people's debts out of them, and his own grew faster than he did. He fought honestly, worked honestly and honestly didn't understand how it was being counted. Then he learned not to ask. That was the worst of all.
Последнее поручение гильдии: ящики чёрно: The guild's last errand: crates of black sand — “to the grey one, at the third sluice.” Dorn opened his. The sand whispered in the voices of the dead. Dorn closed the lid and refused to carry it. Bugs dragged the crate off, and he was driven into a dead end behind a grate. He sat there a week and scratched on a brick: “Dorn slept here. Debt — 4000. Remaining — 4000.” When the grate was opened, the first thing he said was, “I'm the one who brought that filth here.”
Гильдия воров прячется у пирамиды под Мо: The Thieves' guild hides by a pyramid beneath Morroc, and its trial is just one: gather mushrooms on the guild farm without getting caught by the guards. Dorn was caught on his very first step — you can see him from Sograt. The second time he just walked in, gathered mushrooms and gave the guard his lunch: “I'm not hiding, I'm working.” Set let him through for the nerve and put the lunch on his debt. Zara passed the same day — nobody saw her. Then she came back and silently pulled Dorn out of the thorns. He still owes her for that too.
Красть Дорна в гильдии учили, но он отка: The guild tried to teach Dorn to steal, but he refused: “I don't take, I carry.” So the old bouncer at the guild door showed him something else — a double strike, two fists almost at once. “The first is for you. The second for whoever's behind you.” Back then no one was behind Dorn, and his second punch came out limp for a long time. Then Zara came along, then the squad. Now Dorn's second punch is stronger than his first. The bouncer, they say, meant it that way.
Гильдия ассасинов прячется в оазисе без: The Assassin guild hides in a nameless oasis, and you must reach it unseen. Dorn is never unseen. He crossed the sands by day, standing tall, with a flask of milk. The guards saw him a mile off — and didn't raise the alarm: they couldn't believe anyone would do that. The guild master gave him katars in place of a debt. Dorn set a condition: a fair fight, no stabbing in the back. “An Assassin who doesn't stab in the back,” said the master. “I'll get there from the front,” said Dorn. He does.
На корабле Дрейка Дорн узнал гильдейские: On Drake's ship Dorn recognized guild knots: he'd tied hundreds of them himself. The sand was leaving by sea. An Assassin Cross could cut the whole bundle in one stroke, but Dorn untied them one by one, checking the crates and leaving none of the old lashings. “So nobody carries it again,” he told Bran. Courier work used to be an excuse: what was inside wasn't his business. Now he answered for what he left behind, too. Bran wrote nothing down.
В башне Альдебарана Дорн застрял в шесте: In the Al De Baran tower, Dorn got stuck in a gear. Assassin Cross training said strike first; he put away his katars so as not to hit those pulling him out. Vika greased his shoulder, Greta hauled on a strap, Bran counted the turns. Dorn was the first to laugh. That night he realized: in the guild strangers laughed at him; here, his own did. In the morning he asked Bran to show him the math. Strength doesn't change the size of a passage; he wouldn't make his friends take risks for his stubbornness again.
В Гласт Хейме Дорн увидел мёртвый караул: In Glast Heim, Dorn saw the dead watch: knights keeping their oath, though their master had been the first to let the enemy in. By the priests lay crates from that same sand he'd hauled through the sewers. Dorn sat on the steps: “They owe less than I do. And still they stand.” Then he got up and went first, but agreed with Alan where he'd stop. An Assassin Cross doesn't have to charge in alone. He wanted to come back and dismantle the crates left behind, not leave his comrades one more debt.
У врат Нифльхейма Дорн сказал: «Я никому: At the gates of Niflheim, Dorn said, “I don't owe anyone anymore. And I'm still here.” Then he wiped the figures off the brick in the sewers himself. A messenger came to the tavern: Morroc has cracked, red light from the pavement, Set is gone, guild men are carrying a heavy crate. Dorn finished his milk and checked his katars. The Assassin Cross no longer took orders from whoever held his IOU. “Where to?” Now he wasn't going to have a debt written off. Home can't be handed to those hauling sand again.
Разбойники Комодо испытаний не устраиваю: Comodo's Rogues don't hold trials: find the entrance to the caves above the sea and talk the guard round. Dorn found the entrance by smell — it smelled of goats, like his mother's by the well. The guard turned out to be an old shepherd. They talked goats until morning: what to feed them, how to milk them, why the black one is more stubborn than the white. At dawn the guard rolled the stone aside: “Anyone who talks about goats like that won't hurt his own.” By then Dorn had paid off his debt to Morroc himself. Now he chooses whom to serve. He chose — his own.
В трюме Дорн нашёл гильдейскую флягу со: In the hold, Dorn found a guild flask of soured milk. Someone else had been carrying it to their mother too and never made it. A Stalker knows how to take what's useful without lingering; Dorn lingered, washed out the flask and checked the seam before pouring in fresh. “So at least someone makes it,” he told Bran, and took a sip himself. The squad grinned. Dorn saved some for the road: now he decides what he carries and for whom. Neither the guild brand nor the old debt decides that.
В архиве Альдебарана Дорн смотрел не на: In the Al De Baran archive, Dorn looked not at the vanished name but at the torn edge. “A thief would cut it with a knife. This was torn by hand. In a hurry. Scared.” A Stalker can tell a careful trail from panic; he asked them to keep the scraps while they searched for a copy. The archivist looked at him with respect and counted the scrolls. Dorn didn't take offense: you can trust and still check. He used to use his fists to make people stop suspecting him. Now he helped find what had been hidden.
В Гласт Хейме Дорн выбил меч у мёртвого: In Glast Heim, Dorn knocked the sword from a dead knight's hand. The knight stayed at his post. A Stalker could have taken the weapon; Dorn put it back, after making sure the squad had already passed. “You owe less than I do. Stand with your sword.” The oath held the knight more firmly than the master who let the enemy in. Finding empty sand crates by the priests, Dorn burned every one. He left his own not a single old burden. Disarming someone and humiliating the one holding his post are different things.
После вести о трещине в Морроке двое гил: After the news of the crack in Morroc, two guild men offered Dorn Set's place: everyone remembers the courier who refused to carry the crate. The Stalker heard them out, hands in plain sight. “I paid off my debt so I wouldn't serve under compulsion. I serve whom I've chosen.” He nodded at the squad. The guild men left with nothing. Dorn checked his flask and stood up: “Where to?” South. He'd been offered other people's debts and power over them; he preferred people he could help without an IOU.
Ирис росла при казармах Пронтеры: мать с: Iris grew up by the barracks of Prontera: her mother washed the knights' cloaks, and the girl knew the order's code before her alphabet. At fourteen she came to the parade ground on her own, at fifteen she held the line better than the boys, at seventeen she was given the order's shield. The first week she slept hugging it. The shield was heavy, with Prontera's crest, and it seemed to Iris that the whole world could hide behind it.
Бой был в холмах у Излуда. Строй отходил: The battle was in the hills near Izlude. The line was falling back, and three wounded were left beyond it — Iris could see and hear them. The code said: hold the line, never drop the shield. You can't carry three with a shield. Iris dropped the shield, carried out one, went back, carried out the second, went back for the third. When she returned to the line without a shield, bloody to the elbows, the sergeant said, “You dropped your shield.” He said nothing about the wounded.
Суд ордена был коротким. Щит рыцаря не б: The order's court was brief. A knight never drops the shield — Iris knew the code better than the judges. She was expelled, and the shield returned to her as a mere object: “as a keepsake.” Iris walked out the barracks gate, leaned the shield against the wall and left. The next day she bought a two-hander from the smith on the market square — with all her money. The smith asked why a girl needed such a big sword. “So there's no hand left for a shield,” she replied.
Испытание мечников в Излуде — столбы над: The Swordman trial in Izlude is posts over the sea. Iris was fifteen, and she ran them with a sack of sand on her shoulders. No one asked her to. The instructor had simply told the Novices that in battle the wounded are the first to be abandoned — and Iris decided to see if she could hold a wounded man above the water. She could. She never fell once. One-eyed master Rolf chalked on the wall: “Iris: not once.” He asked why the sack. “So I won't have to choose later,” she replied. The entry is still there.
Первый настоящий приём Ирис показал Роль: Rolf showed Iris her first real technique: a strike that makes a ring of fire flare around the Swordman. “So the enemy backs off from the fallen,” he said. Iris practiced until her boots began to smoke. Years later, already expelled, she sat on the Izlude pier watching a loud boy fall into the water for the ninth time. “Your feet,” she said, and left. The boy was Alan. He didn't recognize her. He did recognize the entry on the wall — and for a long time couldn't believe it was the same Iris.
Рыцари Пронтеры испытывают боем, где гла: Prontera's knights test with a battle where the point isn't to win but to leave none of your own behind. Iris carried every “wounded” out from under the wooden swords, one after another, with her two-hander on her back. The examiner was the very sergeant who had once said “you dropped your shield.” He was silent to the end, then recited the order's motto: “The shield is for another.” “That's why I gave it away,” said Iris. She wasn't given a shield. She was given a knight's two-hander. The sergeant brought the scabbard himself.
Наёмник в «Двух колоколах» хвастал, что: A mercenary at the Two Bells was bragging that he never retreats. Iris led him out to a sandbag: carry the wounded with a sword in hand, under arrows, without dropping him. He couldn't. The Lady Knight didn't finish him off with mockery: she showed him where to cover his burden with a two-hander and when to call for relief. “That's why people retreat. With a burden.” In the morning he came for a second lesson. Iris gave him the time before her watch. Strength you can't teach to another saves too few.
На рынке Ирис встретил третий из вынесен: At the market, Iris ran into the third of the wounded she'd carried out. Now he has a shop, a wife and a son on his shoulders; he teaches his son not to abandon his own. The Lady Knight wouldn't take money, but she took an apple from the boy. That evening she smiled and didn't explain why. The order that expelled her recorded the dropped shield. Before her stood the result of that same choice, which the code never counted. She cut the apple in two with her new pupil, starting the lesson without words.
В Гласт Хейме Ирис нашла жетоны отряда Г: In Glast Heim, Iris found the tags of Garret's squad. She didn't hand them over at once: the captain had to name the people he'd left here himself. When he confessed, she poured every tag into his palms and dug beside him until dawn. The Lord Knight kept not a single one as proof of merit. Garret laid a tag in each grave. For the first time in years, Iris took off a lighter belt. The names had returned to their own; she no longer had to carry them in place of a burial.
Орден, изгнавший Ирис, пригласил её учит: The order that cast Iris out invited her to teach its novices. The Lord Knight came without a shield and demanded no apology before the lesson. She laid down a sack for a wounded man: carry him behind the line, the whole formation together. The first time they dropped him, the second they got him out, the tenth — without a single shout. That same sergeant took off his helmet up in the gallery. Iris pretended not to notice. What mattered more to her was that tomorrow none of these novices would have to choose between a comrade and fear of the rulebook.
Орден Креста позвал Ирис сам. Испытание: The Order of the Cross called on Iris itself. The trial: a fast and a night at the tombs of fallen brothers. By morning the abbot brought her a shield bearing the cross. Iris hadn't held a shield since that trial. Her hand remembered the weight before her head did — and Iris nearly let go. “They cast you out for dropping your shield to save three,” the abbot said. “We give it to you to save everyone.” Iris took it. The first night she didn't sleep hugging it, the way she had at seventeen. She just stood it beside the bed. It was calmer that way.
Гаррет остановился у жетонов Ирис: «Трои: Garret stopped by Iris's tags: “Three?” — “Three.” He paid for dinner and left. The Paladin's shield hadn't won her back her place in the old order or made that choice any easier. But the captain didn't need it explained how heavy it is to carry the living past the fallen. Since then they greet each other with a nod. Bruno calls it their silent conversations. Iris saves Garret a spot by the wall: a man who carried someone out sometimes needs his back covered too.
Первый жетон Ирис отнесла матери стражни: Iris took the first tag to a guardsman's mother in Izlude. Leaving back then had been easier. Now, in the evenings, the Paladin sorts through the tags and reads a short prayer of the Order of the Cross for each name. Bruno stops clattering the dishes. Iris checks the records of places, so that one day she can bring not just metal but an answer — where the person lies. Her belt jingles as she walks. “That way the ones I haven't found yet can hear me.” She promises families nothing she doesn't yet know.
У могил отряда Гаррета Ирис стояла со щи: At the graves of Garret's squad, Iris stood with her shield: Raydrics prowled nearby while the captain worked on his knees. The Paladin held the passage, not hurrying the burial or asking him to help her. Once she had carried out the wounded; now she covered a man who needed to stay until the last tag. Garret raised his head: “Thank you, sister.” For the first time Iris didn't correct him that she wasn't of the order. Belonging can be proven by standing guard, even if it was once taken away by decree.
После Нифльхейма Ирис взяла старый щит у: After Niflheim, Iris took the old shield from the door of the Two Bells. The hall fell silent. She had the smith engrave a cross and put it back: “Whoever takes it carries out the wounded. And I'll help.” The Paladin didn't turn the shield into a monument to her return. She checked the straps so the next one could actually lift it. Bruno dusts it on Fridays. Iris makes sure the doorway stays clear: a promise has to work in a hurry, too.
Дед Отто возил из Альберты рыбу — от нег: Otto's grandfather hauled fish from Alberta — he smelled of the sea even in his coffin. His father hauled cloth and died with a measuring stick in his hand. Otto drove a horse at seven, haggled with customs at twelve, and inherited the cart at sixteen. “She's older than you and smarter,” his father said. “Listen to her creak.” Otto listens to this day. Creak number three — rain's coming. Creak number seven — the buyer's lying.
Тележку Отто зовёт «она» и никогда по им: Otto calls the cart “her” and never by name: only she knows her name. Her wheels don't match — one is Grandpa's, two are Father's, one was bought in Payon from a smith who turned out to be a crook. Her sides are patched with barrel staves from every port in Midgard. On the road Otto sleeps under her, and in the rain beside her, covering her with his cloak. People ask why not the other way around. Otto explains: she's older.
У Южных ворот Пронтеры люк стоял без кры: At Prontera's South Gate a manhole stood uncovered, and the horse saw a rat. The cart went down into the sewers with all the goods. Otto sold the horse that same day: “traitor.” He went down after it with a lantern and followed the trail — a wheel, a plank, a nail. The bugs had carried off the nails — shiny, if you please. Otto is collecting them back: he knows every nail by sight. “Otto doesn't give up,” he informed the squad. About himself, in the third person. For weight.
Испытание торговцев Отто, альбертинец в: Otto, a third-generation Albertan, took the merchant trial on his own cart: a parcel across half the world, and back with a Kafra receipt. On the way out of Alberta a girl from Prontera with a frying pan hopped on and haggled the fare down to zero within three miles. Otto haggled all the way to Morroc. He lost. Kafra made out the receipt to both of them. He never asked his fellow traveler's name, but he remembered creak number seven: the whole way she lied that it was the last of her money. In the Prontera sewers, he recognized her.
Первый настоящий приём мастер гильдии в: The guild master in Alberta showed Otto his first real technique on an empty barrel: get the cart rolling and ram the enemy with it. Otto was horrified. Hit with her? With HER? He stood over the cart for half an hour in silence. Then he rocked her side. She creaked — creak number five, one Otto had never heard before. “She agrees,” he translated. The barrel burst into splinters. The cart — not a scratch. That evening Otto greased her axles with the best oil and apologized. Just in case.
В Эйнброхе кузнеца испытывают так: выкуй: In Einbroch, a blacksmith is tested like this: forge a blade the senior master can't break. Otto forged an axle. The master hit it with a hammer, bent it, hung an anvil from it — the axle didn't budge. “That's not a blade.” — “A blade breaks,” said Otto. “An axle — never. It carries the whole load.” The master thought it over and stamped his mark. Otto later built a new cart from that axle, with iron sides. He didn't abandon the old one: she rolls alongside, on a rope. She's jealous, Otto says.
An orc patrol near Geffen stopped Otto. A club's handle had cracked. The Mastersmith didn't haggle: he bound it with a hoop and handed it back, checking that the edge wouldn't cut the palm. The orc laid dried meat on the cart. Work is a language everyone understands, they teach in Einbroch. Otto considers the deal fair, though the meat is tough. A mended handle didn't make them friends, but the next caravan won't be met as people who don't care about someone else's road.
Из Альдебарана Отто впервые повёз не тов: From Al De Baran, Otto hauled people instead of goods for the first time. Vika slept on the sacks, Dorn held the side on the turns, Bran counted potholes. The Mastersmith heard the seventh creak and stopped to tighten a fastening: living cargo can't be delivered “almost intact.” “Best cargo in three generations.” He didn't take a copper. He wrote out an invoice for form's sake; it hangs framed in the tavern. In it Otto listed not a price but every passenger. Not one was lost.
Отто прибил к тележке «Не продаётся», ни: Otto nailed “Not for sale” to the cart, and below it, “Expensive.” A merchant from Juno offered a new one, iron, with springs. The Mastersmith thought and rocked her side: the first creak, the one that sounded when his father sat him on the driver's bench. He turned the deal down. Then he checked the axles: memory doesn't excuse bad iron when you're hauling your own. The merchant left, Otto stayed to repair. He'll keep the cart not instead of reliability but together with it, as long as his hands hold out.
У врат Нифльхейма Тео пел дорогу назад,: At the gates of Niflheim, Teo sang the road back while Otto waited with the cart. “Someone has to get them home.” The Mastersmith went over both wheels, laid out soft bedding and left the tailgate free. Teo went hoarse; Otto didn't ask how long to wait. When the squad came out of the fog, he helped each one up, and only then kicked away the chock. The cart creaked in a way he didn't know. Otto decided: “Home.” For this cargo, it isn't the clock that sets the delivery time.
Алхимиков Альдебарана испытывают зельем: Al De Baran tests its alchemists with a flawless potion and an explanation for every drop. Otto explained like a merchant: “This drop is for weight. This one's for color — buyers love green.” The examiner sighed, but the potion was exact. Otto's first real flask was acid. At the market it didn't sell at all. But the bugs in the sewers scattered from it. Otto thought it over and loaded the cart with acid instead of goods. Fewer buyers. Fewer enemies, too.
Отто пишет матери в Альберту: «Жив. Теле: Otto writes to his mother in Alberta: “Alive. Rebuilding the cart. Found a wheel.” She asked whether it wasn't time to come home. The Biochemist spent three days choosing an answer. Potions and cargo must be delivered by the living; someone has to watch the flasks while the squad sleeps. “The squad's here. Someone has to haul them.” Along with the letter he sent a spare wheel, without taking the reserve off the cart. His mother planted flowers in it. Otto chose to stay, but he didn't make her wait without word.
Замок архива Альдебарана держался сто ле: The lock on Al De Baran's archive had held for a hundred years; the key was long lost. Otto covered the lower scrolls, measured out three drops and waited for the iron to crumble. A Biochemist answers for what lies behind the door, too. The archivist grabbed for an invoice; Otto wrote a counter-invoice for the opening. They settled with no debt, and the squad was let in to the chronicle. Bran called the deal pointless. Otto put the flask away: the paper was intact, the door open. That was what he'd meant to buy.
В Гласт Хейме первая склянка показала От: In Glast Heim, his first flask taught Otto: the dead don't feel acid, but the damp had already eaten their plate. The Biochemist started aiming at buckles and straps, never spilling the mixture under his own people's feet. The knights were left standing without armor. Dorn laughed; Otto gathered the buckles after neutralizing the residue. Good brass will come in handy. He didn't waste potions on pain the enemy can't feel, and he didn't leave his comrades a dangerous road behind the stripped iron.
У врат Нифльхейма Отто ждал на дороге, к: At the gates of Niflheim, Otto waited on the road Teo held with his voice. In the cart: healing potions instead of acid; the Biochemist had brewed them for a week with almost no sleep. “Selling?” — “These goods are for our own.” He arranged the flasks by effect so tired hands wouldn't make mistakes. When the squad came out of the fog, he gave away every last one. The cart creaked in a new way: “Home,” Otto decided. And for the first time in a week, he let someone else take the reins.
Первое заклинание Кай сотворил в шесть л: Kai cast his first spell at six: he wanted to light the candle on his birthday cake. The candle, the cake, the tablecloth and half his father's beard went up in flames. His father laughed while putting it out. His mother took her son to Geffen Tower that same year: “Let them teach him before he teaches himself.” Lira was taken along with him — to keep an eye on him. She was five. She keeps an eye on him to this day.
Ночью в библиотеке Гефенской башни было: At night the Geffen Tower library was cold, and Kai wanted tea. He warmed the kettle with his palms, as he'd been taught. The kettle boiled. Then it caught fire. Then — the shelves, the scrolls, the stairs and the roof. In the morning Kai stood on the ashes with a kettle that did indeed have tea in it. Hot. He offered the rector a cup. The rector billed him an amount the size of the tower. That's not a figure of speech, that's a figure.
Башня послала Кая и Лиру записывать обря: The Tower sent Kai and Lira to record orc rites. Shamans toss herbs into the fire — Kai tossed a bit more. Three stretches of palisade burned down: Lira put out two, Greta the third, with a frying pan. The orcs surrounded Kai, and for the first time in his life he didn't know what to say. Lira spoke for him — in Orcish, which she'd studied at night. The shaman laughed. Kai is still sure it was a success.
Испытание гильдии магов в Гефене — смеша: The Geffen mages' guild trial: mix a solution by a recipe where one extra drop turns the exam into a fire. Carved above the door: “Think first. Then cast.” Kai didn't read it. He added a drop “to be sure,” and the examiner's table burst into flame. At the next table Lira mixed her solution perfectly, silently poured half into her brother's flask and put out the table with her sleeve. The examiner pretended he'd seen nothing. Unlike Kai, he had read the motto above the door.
Первую настоящую молнию Кай пустил во дв: Kai loosed his first real lightning in the Geffen Tower courtyard — at a straw dummy. He hit the dummy, the rack behind it, the weathervane on the roof and the dovecote. The pigeons were fine; the weathervane points north to this day. The magister said: “Lightning always finds a way. Your job is to find it before the lightning does.” Lira stood nearby with a bucket. Since that day a bucket has always stood next to Kai: first Lira set it out, then the librarians, then Bruno. Kai pretends not to notice.
Волшебника в Гефене испытывают поединком: Geffen tests a Wizard with a duel against the elements in the tower cellar. Two conditions: win, and don't destroy the tower. The librarians added a third — don't burn the books — and, just in case, stood with buckets on every floor. Kai fought for an hour. His lightning landed squarely on target; the fire never crept up the walls. When he came out, sooty and whole, the librarians stood with full buckets and couldn't believe it. The Tower forgave him the library: it needs a storm more than books. The buckets weren't put away right away.
Кай хотел согреть отмель Излуда, а молни: Kai wanted to warm the Izlude shallows, but the lightning went into the sea. By morning it smelled of fish soup. The fishermen first chased him with oars, then sat down to eat. Lira paid for forty baskets. The High Wizard still called it a great experiment, but he went to tally the damage himself and wrote down the depth at which the spell had slipped. He gave his sister back a calculation, not an excuse. The stronger the storm, the wider the circle of those who pay if he once again aims only at his own idea.
Прошение Кая о долге сгорело на третьей: Kai's petition about the debt burned up on the third line, the second on the fifth. The High Wizard wrote the third in gloves, with Lira behind him. The reply: the debt was cut by a third for her field reports filed under his name. Kai went to argue and came back quiet. He didn't set anything on fire all evening. In the morning he took a clean sheet: the next observations would be signed by whoever made them. For years his sister had paid not just in silver. That was harder to admit than taming a storm.
Лира ушла вперёд, а огонь в руках Кая вы: Lira went on ahead, and the fire in Kai's hands grew beyond measure. This was exactly what the High Wizard had feared: his sister's gone, and everyone will pay for the mistake. He didn't call for her. He breathed in, clenched his fists the way she'd taught him, and snuffed the flame. Then he checked for sparks left at his comrades' feet. Bran wrote: “Kai put it out himself.” Kai asked him to tear out the page. Bran refused. For the first time the notebook held not destruction but a strike held back — and Kai wasn't used to seeing it.
Как не сжечь библиотеку: How Not to Burn a Library
В Гефене Кай читал первокурсникам «Как н: In Geffen, Kai gave first-years a lecture: “How Not to Burn a Library.” He came with a bucket and told them about the tea, the palisade and the fish soup. The students laughed until he named who had paid and put out the fire each time. Then the High Wizard lit a palm-sized storm and snuffed it himself. Lira sat in the back row with no ice in her pocket. Kai left the bucket by the lectern: skill doesn't cancel caution. The next student shouldn't have to learn on someone else's library.
В Академии Юно испытание — не заклинание: At Juno Academy the trial isn't a spell but a debate: prove to the council that you know why magic works. When Kai gets nervous, his sleeves smoke. He argued for three hours and didn't let out a single spark. His main point was simple: “Fire always wants more than it's given. I know. I'm the same.” The council laughed, then went quiet, then accepted him — on one condition: burn only enemies. The Academy's motto: “To understand is to win without fire.” So far Kai has understood half.
Кай попросил Лиру научить льду. Она поня: Kai asked Lira to teach him ice. She realized he meant it. For a week by the well his ice came out warm, then wet; on the eighth day a snowflake held. For the first time, the Juno Professor learned from his sister something other than how to fix his own mess. “So this is how you feel all the time.” Lira turned away. The snowflake melted; Kai said it was on purpose and didn't push the joke. In the margins he wrote down not only the formula but how many times his sister had patiently started over.
В башне Альдебарана Кай наложил огонь на: In the Al De Baran tower, Kai enchanted Alan's sword with fire. The Professor first asked whether the hilt would hold, and showed how to stop the enchantment. Alan roared with delight: the guardian melted, the sword survived. For the first time Kai's fire proved useful in someone else's hands. Lira called it a miracle; the Academy extended his probation. Kai didn't argue: one intact sword isn't enough. He wrote down the heat limit so the next fighter wouldn't have to rely on a miracle.
В соборе Гласт Хейма Кай увидел детские: In the Glast Heim cathedral, Kai saw children's names on the pews and Bran with his notebook. A gathered storm would have burned both those coming at the squad and what Bran had stayed behind for. The Professor let it go and struck one at a time, leaving the pews intact. The work went slower; he asked Alan to hold the passage. Afterwards he told Lira: “Winning without fire is about what's behind the enemies.” Every letter survived. For the first time Kai didn't pick the fastest way to prove his strength.
После Нифльхейма Кай сам написал в Юно:: After Niflheim, Kai wrote to Juno himself: “Held the road through the fog with fire, set nothing alight.” Gloves, window, bucket under the desk; Lira only checked the spelling. Probation over. The Professor reread the reply three times and singed a corner: “As a keepsake.” Lira didn't put it out. Kai put the letter away and sat down to finish writing the spell's limits. Next time someone else will hold the road; they'll need an honest calculation, not a story about Kai.
Лиру отдали в Гефенскую башню в пять лет: Lira was sent to Geffen Tower at five — to keep an eye on her brother. She couldn't write yet, but she could already put out fires: with sand, water, a blanket, a word. A word worked best. In the Tower they called her “that one's sister.” Lira didn't mind. She learned every ice rune by age ten, because the water ran out, and Kai didn't.
Лира полюбила лёд не сразу. Сначала он б: Lira didn't love ice right away. At first it was just a remedy for her brother. Then she noticed: ice is honest. It holds while it's cold and doesn't pretend to be anything else. Fire always wants more than it's given; ice takes exactly as much as it needs. Lira set her first ice sigil on the door of their room. It stood for seven years. Kai burned through the wall next to it to get in.
Когда Кай сжёг библиотеку, Лира неделю н: When Kai burned down the library, Lira didn't sleep for a week: she froze the ashes so they wouldn't crumble and pulled bindings out of them. She saved forty-two scrolls. The rector called it a miracle and sent the bill — to her brother. Lira silently laid three years of her savings on the rector's desk. The rector took them. Kai doesn't know about it, and Lira will never tell. The debt didn't get smaller, but she feels calmer this way.
Экзамен гильдии магов в Гефене Лира сдал: Lira passed the Geffen mages' guild exam the same day as her brother, at the next table. Her solution — exactly by the recipe, to the drop. Then, out of the corner of her eye, she saw Kai reach for the extra one “to be sure,” and already had her sleeve ready. The table flared, Lira put it out, poured half her solution for her brother and sat back down. The examiner said nothing. That evening her “fix after Kai” list gained a line: “exam.” Lira crossed it out at once. With a single stroke.
Первое настоящее заклинание Лиры — лёд,: Lira's first real spell: ice that locks a target in place. The magister told her to freeze a dummy. Lira froze the flame on the sleeve of her brother, who happened to be walking by. The flame set like glass and shattered. Kai was unharmed and didn't even notice. “The target was chosen correctly,” the magister said after a pause. Lira understood something important: ice holds more than just enemies. Ever since, she's kept a piece of ice in her pocket. Just in case — that is, for Kai.
Стена вместо удара: A Wall Instead of a Strike
Поединок со стихиями в подвале Гефенской: Lira began her duel with the elements in the Geffen Tower cellar not with a strike, but with a wall. A fire spirit beat against the ice for an hour and didn't get through. “The exam is about power,” the examiner reminded her. “There it is,” said Lira. The Tower made her a Wizard: her ice holds an entire squad. All that time Kai stood by the cellar door with a bucket, waiting for his sister. For the first time in his life, he was the one holding it. Lira came out, saw, and laughed so hard the wall behind her cracked.
В метель под Альдебараном Лира подняла л: In a blizzard near Al De Baran, Lira raised an ice wall not for her brother's sake. The High Wizard chose its height and curve herself; behind the wall the squad could light a fire without abandoning the watch. Kai set nothing alight, so as not to get in the way. Lira left a gap for the shift change, then stroked the ice like a cat: “Mine.” The wall stood till morning. For the first time her power served a plan that didn't begin with the word “fix.” And she didn't have to stop looking out for the others.
В бою Лира почти шёпотом сказала: «Назад: In battle Lira said, almost in a whisper: “Back.” The whole line stepped back; a column crashed down where they'd stood. “The ice cracked,” she explained. The High Wizard listened to her own supports before the roar of the enemy. Kai had always heard her through a blaze; now everyone did. That evening she showed Alan the thin crack and agreed on a retreat signal. She didn't want to guess for the whole squad every time. A quiet order needs people who understand it, too.
Башня поручила Каю дело без сестры. Лира: The Tower gave Kai a job without his sister. Lira packed a bucket, gloves, ice in a cloth — and stayed at the gate. The High Wizard could shield a squad with a wall; a day without watching her brother was harder. She sat over cold tea but didn't follow. In the evening Kai came back sooty and handed back the untouched ice. Lira cried in front of him. He'd managed on his own. Her care could finally stop being a watch she wasn't allowed to leave.
Лира вычеркнула последнюю строку «почини: Lira crossed out the last line of “fix after Kai”: they'd repaired Bruno's roof together. She didn't start a new list. Her paper, “Ice That Holds the Line,” went to Geffen — with passages for the wounded and shift calculations, not just blizzard power. It was accepted under Lira's name. Below, Kai scrawled: “Tested on myself,” leaving a scorch mark. The High Wizard didn't remove it. In this paper her brother was a witness, not the cause. That's more honest.
В Академии Юно Лиру испытывали спором: о: At Juno Academy, Lira was tested by debate: explain to the council why magic works. She covered ice in ten minutes. Then the council asked about fire — just in case, for completeness. Lira spoke for an hour. She explained fire better than any fire mage: how it grows, where it feels cramped, what it fears and when to call it by name. The council exchanged glances. “How do you know all this?” — “I've studied it my whole life,” said Lira. “Its name is Kai.”
Воздушный пузырь для корабля Лира вычисл: Lira calculated the air bubble for the ship: the squad's breathing, the water's warmth, the melt rate. The Professor allotted half an hour, plus a separate twenty-two minutes “if Kai warms it.” He did. The bubble held exactly through the reserve; Lira demanded they surface without argument, though she wanted to explore more. Knowledge isn't an answer but a reserve, they say in Juno. The margin note with the correction for her brother stayed. She kept it not as a reproach: the calculation is there so everyone comes back.
В Альдебаране Лира записывала поломки вр: In Al De Baran, Lira recorded breakdowns of time: clocks running backwards, a baker baking yesterday's bread again, Kai being surprised by the bell all over again. She crossed out the last one: her brother had been surprised before, too. The Professor checked every observation with the townsfolk rather than declaring their memory a mistake. In a week — twelve pages. She gave them to the archivist and kept a copy. For the first time he remembered the day. Fixing the world starts with describing it; someone else's yesterday doesn't belong to whoever can write it down.
В Гласт Хейме Лира не смогла снять рогат: In Glast Heim, Lira couldn't remove the horned mark from a knight. The Professor stopped trying before spending the strength the living needed. While they buried the fallen, she understood: not a spell, but a forgotten oath. Spells are lifted; oaths are remembered. She wrote it in one line and showed Garret. She didn't cross it out: “This one we'll cross out together.” Admitting the limit of her method proved more useful than promising the squad one more spell.
После Нифльхейма Лира проспала четырнадц: After Niflheim, Lira slept fourteen hours at the Two Bells. The first line on her personal list had long been “get some sleep.” For the first time the Professor trusted her brother with the watch at the door: Kai sat with a bucket and shushed even Teo, twice. When she woke, she crossed the line out with a single stroke. She hasn't come up with the second one yet. She didn't turn rest into new work. The next calculation needs a clear head; life needs the right not to know in advance what to do tomorrow.
Отец Мэйлин, пайонский лесничий, научил: Meilin's father, a Payon forester, taught her to read tracks before letters. At four she could tell a fox from a dog, at six — three kinds of fox, at eight — the track of a man who lies: he steps more carefully than he needs to. Letters came later and grudgingly. Meilin still reads slowly. Tracks — faster than anyone in Payon.
Первый лук отец выстрогал ей из орешника: Her father whittled her first bow from hazel while she still ate with her hands. Meilin learned to hold it properly before a spoon — her mother complained that her daughter aimed at the porridge. Her father taught: shoot only when you know at what. Payon Forest remembers who shoots for nothing. Meilin never once shot for nothing. Except once, at nine, at the neighbor's rooster. The rooster forgave her. Her father — not right away.
Десять лет назад лес Пайона горел три дн: Ten years ago, Payon Forest burned for three days. Her father fought the fire with everyone else, and Meilin carried water in her hat. On the third day, by the fox dens, she found a burned fox cub — alone. She nursed it all winter. In spring it went into the forest and didn't look back. Her father said: that's how it should be, if you healed it. Meilin still greets every red shadow in Payon. What if it's him.
Испытание гильдии лучников Пайона Мэйлин: Meilin passed the Payon archers' guild trial by lunch: the forest is home to her, and she knew every deadwood tree by heart. On the way back, in a hollow, a boy from Prontera sat over a map with a notebook, counting the steps to a forest he was already standing in. Meilin led him to the deadwood, said “don't cut the living,” and left. By tradition an archer carves their name on their bow. Meilin didn't: in Payon, foresters' daughters sign a bow once it's earned. The guild mistress didn't argue.
Первый настоящий приём Мэйлин не понрави: Meilin didn't like her first real technique: a rain of arrows over the whole enemy line. Her father had taught otherwise — shoot only when you know at what. “The rain is for when you know everything,” said the guild mistress. “That there are none of your own up ahead.” Meilin practiced on fallen leaves: she loosed the rain so as not to touch a single living leaf on a branch. Within a month she touched none. The mistress said that's impossible. Meilin said the forest helps. Both were right.
Пустое место на луке: The Empty Spot on the Bow
Охотники Пайона послали Мэйлин в Хьюджел: The Payon hunters sent Meilin to Hugel: three tracks, a trap, a falcon. She read the tracks without crouching, set the trap so the forest didn't notice. But the falcon wouldn't come. It circled all day and wouldn't land. Meilin didn't call. On the second morning it landed on its own — on her bow, on the empty spot by the grip left for her father's name. “The falcon chooses its master,” the hunters said. Meilin sees it differently: it chose the spot. Now, when she searches for the white wolf, the falcon flies ahead.
Мэйлин проходит по лесу, не вспугивая пт: Meilin walks through the forest without startling the birds; only a drawn bowstring gives her away. Sniper training added to her father's step the choice of a position from which she can also see her own. In the tavern she won a bet with Dorn: walked past, took his milk and came back unnoticed. She returned the mug: “A fox would have noticed.” Then she showed him where the floor creaks. She wanted more than winning the bet: on watch, Dorn has to hear what he can't see.
На северной дороге Мэйлин ставила капкан: On the northern road Meilin set traps for pursuers, not for the white wolf. The Sniper left her own people a marked way around. In the morning the wolf went around every trap and left a hare by the last one. The falcon grumbled; Meilin laughed for the first time in a week. Her father used to leave game by her childhood traps just like that: “Don't catch me.” Or: “Eat.” She checked the snares and didn't move them to the wolf's trail. Getting her father's bow back doesn't mean catching the one who guarded her father.
След белого волка уходит к северному тум: The white wolf's trail leads into the northern fog. Meilin isn't afraid of the dead — she saw them sleeping in Payon — but of places where birds don't sing. The Sniper checked her arrows and agreed on a meeting point with the squad: the search gives her no right to vanish without a trace herself. Her father taught her to keep going as long as there's a trail. There is a trail. She goes, but leaves marks for the way back. Whoever searches for a loved one shouldn't make others search for them as well.
Белый волк лёг за костром. Лука при нём: The white wolf lay down beyond the campfire. It didn't have the bow. Meilin took the arrow off the string and gave it half her supper; the Sniper could have had it in her sights, but didn't. The wolf stayed until morning, then went north, looking back. She warned her own people and followed, without drawing the string. The bow won't go anywhere, Meilin says. A friend might. For the first time the trail was not a chase after a thing, but an invitation from the one who had guarded the sleepers in Payon.
Танцовщиц в Комодо испытывают на пляже п: Comodo tests its dancers on the beach under lanterns: dance until dawn, until the band tires. Meilin had never danced. She moved the way she walks through the forest — softly, not breaking a single twig underfoot — and by midnight the drummer began to falter: he couldn't catch her step. By dawn the band gave up. Why does she need this, asked the head of the troupe. “In Payon a song led people into a cave,” said Meilin. “I want to be able to lead them back.” They gave her a tambourine and ankle bells.
Отец спал среди найденных в пещере Пайон: Her father slept among those found in Payon Cave; the white wolf guarded them, then carried his bow north. Meilin follows. Her Comodo Gypsy training made the tambourine a signal to return: in the evenings she keeps the rhythm of footsteps until the last sentry reaches the fire. Not “come to me,” like the lullaby, but “come home.” On the third evening two eyes appeared at the edge of the light. Bran called it a coincidence, Meilin — an audience. She didn't break the rhythm.
У двери «Двух колоколов» Мэйлин нашла св: By the door of the Two Bells, Meilin found a fresh wolf track. It came up to the porch, lingered, and went north. It wasn't hiding: it was checking whether she was here. The Gypsy could have called it with the tambourine, but she wouldn't lure one who comes on his own. Since then she goes out before Bruno and watches the road. Before the evening dance she clears the stools from the passage. Even an audience needs a way back; in Payon a song without such a way led too many off.
В соборе Гласт Хейма мёртвые шли в такт: In the Glast Heim cathedral, the dead marched in time to the lullaby. Meilin stepped out to meet them and shifted her step; the Gypsy's bells struck off the expected rhythm. The first Raydric stumbled, the second crashed into him. Alan managed to cover Vika. Meilin kept going until her own people were through the narrow passage; only then did she catch her breath and straighten a bell. In Comodo that's how you throw off an opponent. Here, what mattered wasn't applause but leaving no one trapped inside someone else's beat.
За краем Мидгарда птицы не пели. Мэйлин: Beyond the edge of Midgard, no birds sang. Meilin struck the tambourine — the first sound in three days — and the white wolf came to the fire without the bow. The Gypsy danced until dawn, as at her trial, leaving him room on the other side of the fire. He didn't leave. In the morning he set off north, looking back; Meilin followed, telling her own people the way. The bow won't go anywhere. But the audience might. Now her step compelled no one: the wolf chose to stay and call her onward himself.
Зару нашли в Морроке на ступенях гильдии: Zara was found in Morroc on the steps of the thieves' guild: no name, no kin, someone else's purse in her fist. She was six. Set took her as his apprentice himself — he liked it when talent came to the doorstep. At ten she could crack any lock in the quarter, at twelve she knew any poison by smell. The fastest, the quietest. Dorn always stomped along beside her — the loudest. They were friends because there was no one else.
Зара приставляет нож к горлу при встрече: Zara puts a knife to your throat when you meet. It's not a threat but a question: “Are you one of us?” That's what the guild taught — trust is tested with steel, not words. Our own don't flinch. Strangers do. Dorn has never flinched once.
