The damp hardens their shells so much that novices' knives go dull on them. An egg doesn't walk or attack — but mandibles poke out through a crack and bite anyone who comes too close. The bugs consider the clutch a dowry and bring it all their shiniest finds.
It does nothing, but beating it takes half a day.
Плевок из тёмной воды: A Spit from the Dark Water
Планктон — полупрозрачный комок, который: Plankton is a translucent lump that sways in the canals' stagnant water and spits acid sludge at anything that makes noise. On its own it's nearly harmless, but the sewer acid eats through bandages and skin, and Plankton always spits at whoever is already wounded. Sergeant Berthold advises novices: “Spitters first, before they find their aim.”
Мозгов нет, а в раненого попадает с перв: No brains, yet it hits the wounded on the first try.
Тару — серая крыса с длинным голым хвост: A Tarou is a grey rat with a long bare tail, the first thing a novice hears in the canals: a rustle, a squeak, and then the whole pack is running down the gutter. Tarous bite at the legs so their prey can't run, and haul scraps to the bugs — they say that's why the bugs leave their nests alone. Wherever it's damp, dark and smells of bread, there are Tarous.
Одна Тару — к хлебу. Десять — к сержанту: One Tarou means bread. Ten mean fetch the sergeant.
Фамилиар — летучая мышь, которая висит п: A Familiar is a bat that hangs beneath the brick vault until something warm passes below. Then it swoops down, bites and flits off into the dark, and the little wound bleeds for a long time. Old mages kept them as messengers — hence the name; wild Familiars have long served no one.
Если над головой тихо — посмотри, кто та: If it's quiet overhead — check who's keeping silent up there.
Самец жука-вора вдвое крупнее рядового ж: The Male Thief Bug is twice as big as an ordinary bug and ten times as mean. Its mandibles bite clean through a spear shaft, and its shell, they say, has a dull sheen from the coppers it hauled to the nest all its life and rubbed against. The male doesn't steal — it guards those who do, and is first to charge at strangers.
Мелкие воруют. Крупные следят, чтобы вор: The small ones steal. The big ones make sure they steal properly.
Самка жука-вора держится позади стаи и о: The Female Thief Bug stays behind the swarm and regurgitates a sweet, sticky mush from everything the bugs dragged down from above. That's enough for wounded bugs to get back up and bite again. While the female lives, the swarm never ends — anyone who has ever cleared the sewers by royal decree knows that.
Бей ту, что кормит. Остальные проголодаю: Hit the one who feeds them. The rest will go hungry on their own.
Вожак жуков — старый самец, раздобревший: The Bug Chieftain is an old male grown fat on sewer coppers. He guards the main clutch in the galleries beneath Prontera and considers everything shiny in the canals a dowry for his eggs. He clacks his mandibles so loudly the echo carries to the third lock. He fights to the end, but once beaten, the first thing he asks is that you leave the eggs alone — the spoons you can take.
«Щёлк… берите ложки… яйца не берите…»: “Clack… take the spoons… leave the eggs…”
Золотой жук-вор живёт в самой глубине ка: The Golden Thief Bug lives in the deepest reaches of Prontera's canals, in a lair piled with coins up to the vault. For centuries townsfolk dropped coppers, rings and buckles into the drains, and the bugs carried it all to him — and he swelled on other people's wealth, growing a shell of fused coins from three kings' reigns. They say he remembers every coin and every coin's owner. Novices who clear the sewers by the king's decree go down to him last: defeating the Golden Bug means earning the title of adventurer by right. This spring he took payment in copper from a man in grey to keep crates of black sand in his lair. He took the crates, and the courier along with them: the man owed a debt, and a debt is almost gold.
Каждая монета в этих стоках — его. И ваш: Every coin in these sewers is his. Yours too. Especially yours.
Воин земли у Гефена: Warrior of the Land near Geffen
Орк-воин носит на поясе топор, а на шее: An Orc Warrior wears an axe on his belt and bone beads around his neck: one bead for every ancestor whose name he remembers. Orcs haven't come out onto the roads in forty years, but they guard their land fiercely: a stranger at the ford gets a roar first, then the axe. Right now the warriors are angry and afraid — their own grandfathers are rising from the mines beneath the village.
Орк не нападает первым. Орк просто первы: An orc never attacks first. An orc just notices first that you already have.
Высший орк из двора вождя: High Orc of the Chief's Court
Высшие орки — самые рослые и старшие вои: High Orcs are the tallest and eldest warriors of the tribe, the chief's guard. Their hides are tanned tough enough to stop an arrow, and they hold the line until the chief orders a retreat. They say a High Orc can stand at the gate for a full day without food — just to keep strangers from the graves.
Стена из шкур, мышц и упрямства. Упрямст: A wall of hide, muscle and stubbornness. The stubbornness is the toughest part.
Орк-лучник стреляет с холма и никогда не: The Orc Archer shoots from the hill and never comes down first. Arrowheads are carved from the bones of prey, and fletching from the feathers of vultures circling the range. Archers consider it shameful to miss a standing target. A running one — not so: a runner, in their view, has already understood everything.
Две стрелы — одна для вас, вторая на слу: Two arrows — one for you, the second in case you didn't get the first.
Орчиха ведёт хозяйство деревни, лечит ра: The Orc Lady runs the village, treats the wounded with herbs and beats out the rhythm of battle on her drum. To her drum, warriors strike faster and feel no wounds. Even the chief doesn't argue with an Orc Lady: she remembers who came to her with a cracked skull and how many times, and reminds them in front of everyone.
Пока бьёт барабан, орк не падает. Упасть: While the drum beats, an orc doesn't fall. Falling would be disrespectful to the drummer.
Стальной чончон — большая муха с панцире: A Steel Chonchon is a large fly with a shell that rings like a kettle. Swarms of Chonchons live near the Geffen fields and in the upper levels of the orc mine; they sting you in the back and fly off before anyone can swat them. Orcs believe Chonchons flock to where there will soon be many dead. This year there are very many of them.
Звенит — значит, близко. Не звенит — зна: If it buzzes — it's close. If it doesn't — it's already on you.
Орк-зомби — мёртвый воин из подземелья п: An Orc Zombie is a dead warrior from the dungeon beneath the village. He was buried with honors, with beads and axe, and lay peacefully while the chiefs' oath held him below. Now he has risen — not woken, but risen from below, as the shamans say. Many zombies wear the same beads as the living warriors above.
Шаман Угра: «Он не злой. Он просто забыл: Ugra the shaman: “He's not evil. He just forgot where he lay down.”
Орк-скелет — предок из самых глубоких яр: An Orc Skeleton is an ancestor from the deepest levels, fallen in wars remembered only in charcoal drawings on the mine walls. No flesh is left on him, but he grips his rusty cleaver firmly and strikes hard enough to knock you down. Orcs say the skeletons are the first guardians of the oath: they lay down before everyone else and rose last.
Он помнит Великую войну. Больше он не по: He remembers the Great War. He remembers nothing else.
Вождь, который уводит своих: The Chief Who Leads His Own Out
Герой орков — вождь-воин, самый сильный: The Orc Hero is the warrior-chief, the strongest and most respected in the tribe. When the old chief went down to the ancestors and didn't return, guarding the land fell to him. He remembers men in iron from twenty winters ago, when they marched past to the castle in the north, ignoring his warning. He meets strangers in the chief's circle: whoever doesn't flee from his roar, he listens to. Defeated by the squad, the first thing he does is lead his wounded up to the surface — and only then guides the humans down to the ancestors. Alan remembered that better than any lesson.
Вождь, который не уводит своих, — не вож: A chief who doesn't lead his own out is no chief.
Орк-лорд — древний вождь, который спусти: The Orc Lord is an ancient chief who went down into the dungeon to renew the ancestors' oath, as custom demands: to hold the dead below for as long as the world stands. Below, a polite man in grey was waiting for him. He placed a horned mark on the chief in black sand — and the chief forgot the oath. Hands that had held the dead for forty winters let go, and the ancestors rose up. When the squad defeated him, the mark went out, and the Orc Lord took up his hold again. Before sleep he managed to say the main thing: the first knot is in the sands. And at that moment, grey ringing smoke slipped out from under the vault.
Tell the chief… I went down. As is proper. I'm holding again.
Будильник — часы, которые однажды решили: An Alarm is a clock that once decided waking people up wasn't enough and grew legs. They roam the lower halls of the tower, ring without warning and kick you in the shins. Al De Baran's alchemists set traps for them for their springs. They say every Alarm has an owner somewhere who never woke up on time.
Будильник не спрашивает, выспались ли вы: An Alarm doesn't ask whether you slept well.
Часы — напольный корпус в рост человека: A Clock is a man-high grandfather case with a heavy pendulum inside. It moves slowly and relentlessly, like time, and likes being rushed just as little. A swing of the pendulum knocks you down and echoes in your bones for a long time. The tower's old masters placed them by the doors: Clocks don't sleep and are never late.
Тик — шаг. Так — удар. Часы не опаздываю: Tick — a step. Tock — a blow. Clocks are never late.
Райдворд — книга из библиотеки башни, ко: A Rideword is a book from the tower library that read itself for so long it learned to fly. Its pages are razor-sharp, and it hurls them at anyone who makes noise in the reading room. Librarians call them “strict volumes” and avoid the fairy-tale shelves: that's where Ridewords are meanest.
В читальне башни не шумят. Шумят один ра: No noise in the tower reading room. You only make noise once.
Панк — пушистый комок в облаке пыли, кот: A Punk is a fluffy ball in a cloud of dust that lives in the tower workshops and zips between gears faster than anyone can oil them. The dust it kicks up stings the eyes and skin. The mechanics are furious, but Punks think that's just how it should be: where there's machinery, there's fun.
Если в мастерской чихают — значит, панк: If someone's sneezing in the workshop — the Punk is already here.
Совиный герцог — большая сова в дорогом: The Owl Duke is a large owl in fine plumage, one of the archive's night wardens. For centuries the tower's owls made sure books didn't go missing and kept strangers out after sunset. The Duke drops from the rafters without a sound and strikes with its talons at the weakest spot. Wounded, it doesn't flee — it preens its feathers: untidiness disgusts it more than pain.
Совы архива помнят каждого читателя. И к: The archive owls remember every reader. And every overdue book.
Старейшина — старый маг башни, который к: The Elder is an old mage of the tower who once repaired its mechanisms and simply stayed among them. He drips oil on squeaking gears and on his charges' wounds, and in a tight spot he winds their injuries back a minute. Who he was when the tower was alive and why he never left — the archive doesn't remember. Or remembers, but keeps quiet.
Капля масла — и снова как новенький. Поч: A drop of oil — good as new. Almost.
Мимик выглядит как сундук из архива: око: A Mimic looks like a chest from the archive: iron-bound, dusty, with a heavy lid. Treasure hunters open it with delight — exactly once. Inside, instead of coins, are teeth and a long tongue. Mimics love vaults with lots of chests, where every new thief is sure that he, at least, will get lucky.
В архиве башни у сундуков есть зубы. Про: In the tower archive, chests have teeth. Confirmed.
Старший над совами архива, строгий, как: Head of the archive owls, strict as the reading-room rules. A week ago the Baron let “a polite gentleman in grey” into the vault — and ever since, caught in a time loop, he's been reliving that night over and over. He no longer lets anyone in: not readers, not the archivist, not the owls. He hides behind his wings as if behind a shield, while his owls strike from the ceiling at those standing in the back.
Мастер башни Альдебарана поклялся записы: The master of the Al De Baran tower swore to record every hour of Midgard, and the Manager is the mechanism that kept that oath after him. It wound the springs, checked the hands and made sure the chronicle never broke off. A week ago a horned mark appeared on it: a polite guest in grey said remembering is painful, and forgetting is kinder. The Manager forgot that it must record. Now it turns time back and erases — and it's stuck in one night, the night Glast Heim fell: three thirteen. When the mark went out, it said “taking up my post” — and the clocks moved forward.
Зелёный богомол размером с телёнка. Стои: A green mantis the size of a calf. It stands still as a dry branch until something tasty walks past. Prontera's mushroom pickers say: if a branch in the labyrinth bows to you — it's not a branch.
It's not praying for you. It's praying for lunch.
Длинный червь, который прячется в земле: A long worm that hides in the ground and sticks out only its stem — exactly like a young sapling. It grabs the legs of anyone who sits down to rest. Janek insists half the “trees” at the third fork are worms.
Не садитесь под молодые деревца. Они гол: Don't sit under young saplings. They're hungry.
Маленький призрак в белом, живёт в дупла: A little ghost in white that lives in the hollows of the Labyrinth Forest. It whispers bargains to travelers: boots that never wear out, a purse that never empties. For a small signature. Baphomet doesn't pay the Whispers — they work on commission.
«Всего одна строчка, и сапоги ваши». Сап: “Just one line, and the boots are yours.” The boots really are nice.
Муха с ладонь, красноглазая, злая. Охоти: A palm-sized fly, red-eyed and vicious. It hunts in swarms and bites where the armor is thinnest. It nests in stumps that repeat — which is why there seem to be endless flies in the forest. There are just a lot of them.
Жужжание в лесу стихло? Значит, вас уже: The buzzing in the forest went quiet? Then you've already been chosen.
Змея, которая ползёт боком и бросается в: A snake that slithers sideways and strikes sideways — from where you least expect it. Its venom isn't deadly, but afterwards the path seems to go uphill all day. In the Labyrinth Forest, mind you, it goes uphill anyway.
Watch your step. And a little to the left.
Мелкий крылатый бес с вилами и папкой. Д: A small winged imp with a pitchfork and a folder. The Deviruchis are Baphomet's office: they deliver papers, collect signatures and patch up the wounded retinue with an “advance” — against future service. They adore seals. They hate blots.
Advance issued. You'll work it off for eternity.
Рогатый чертёнок с косой не по росту — с: A horned little devil with a scythe too big for him — part of Baphomet's retinue. He tumbles about, fights brazenly and is very proud of his master. They say every junior will one day become a senior if he bargains an eternity out of someone. So far, none has managed.
Хозяин велел не драться. Хозяин не узнае: Master said no fighting. Master won't find out.
Серый волк-одиночка, вожак без стаи. Ког: A grey lone wolf, a leader without a pack. Once he led his pack through the forest and struck a deal: the way home in exchange for loyalty. He was shown the way. He can't walk it — he serves. When he howls, the small creatures of the forest gather around him.
Его стая — все, кто слышит вой. Не слуша: His pack is everyone who hears the howl. Don't listen.
Призрачный поринг в колпаке: полупрозрач: A ghostly Poring in a cap: translucent, cold and somehow sad. They say it's a Poring that wasn't finished off before the deal closed. Blades pass through it, and it passes through the line, leaving frost behind.
Поринги обычно смирные. Этот — обычно мё: Porings are usually docile. This one is usually dead.
Девиручи, выросший на бумагах до размеро: A Deviruchi who grew to the size of a wardrobe on paperwork. He keeps the Labyrinth Forest's book of contracts: who signed what, when, and how much they owe. Everyone who has crossed the forest has signed something for someone — the Scribe checks. Resistance, per clause seven, increases the penalty. He stamps his seals on the back row, so the healer gets the message faster.
Подпись здесь, здесь и кровью здесь. Нет: Sign here, here, and in blood here. No? We'll process it by force!
Козлоголовый демон с крыльями и серповид:
A goat-headed demon with wings and a crescent scythe, master of the Labyrinth Forest right outside Prontera. He takes nothing by force — he only buys, and the price is always fair: you just end up paying it longer than the buyer lives. Shamans and priests argue whether he's a demon or a forgotten god. Baphomet himself says he's a notary.

Since the Great War he has kept what opens the gates of Niflheim from this side: not a key, but the consent of the living. For a thousand years no one asked for it. This spring a man in grey came and signed: “I'll open the gates. In return — my wife and son.” Baphomet doesn't fight those who bargain. Only haggling angers him: one tavern keeper from Prontera talked down the price of eternity.
Не деритесь. Торгуйтесь. Все, кто дрался: Don't fight. Bargain. Everyone who fought is standing along the path.
За южными воротами Пронтеры, столицы кор: Beyond the South Gate of Prontera, capital of the kingdom of Rune-Midgard, lie the meadows where guild novices take their first steps. Porings graze here — round pink jellies, harmless until you make them angry. This spring they've gathered in herds and drifted toward the village, and in the forest past the edge something big has woken. Captain Garret is gathering everyone who can hold a weapon.
Каналы и стоки под столицей: Canals and Sewers Beneath the Capital
Под мостовыми Пронтеры тянутся каналы, с: Beneath Prontera's streets run canals, sewers and old locks. By royal decree, novices are sent to clear them of Thief Bugs, which drag everything shiny back to their burrows. This spring other thieves have turned up below — men from Morroc who ship crates of black sand through the canals. The sand is warm and whispers in the voices of the dead. The guard veterans who went down here followed the voices and never came back.
Земли орков к западу от Гефена и подземе: Orc Lands West of Geffen and the Dungeon Beneath the Village
Орки не выходили на дороги сорок лет. Те: Orcs haven't come out onto the roads in forty years. Now their patrols stand at every ford west of Geffen, and from the mines beneath their village rise their ancestors — ancient chiefs in rusted armor. The shamans say the dead rose from below rather than waking on their own: someone broke the oath the chiefs swore after the Great War.
Моррок стоит в песках юга, над тем, о чё: Morroc stands in the southern sands, above something its people would rather forget: a thousand years ago the demon lord the city is named after was sealed here. Pharaohs who swore never to rise sleep in the pyramids. The thieves' guild rules the streets, and Dorn isn't welcome at home.
Деревня лучников в сосновых горах к юго-: An archers' village in the pine mountains southeast of Prontera, with temples, lanterns and a cave where the dead sleep. For centuries the forest's fox spirit sang them a lullaby. This spring people are leaving the village at night of their own accord — following the voices of loved ones long buried.
У порта Излуд, под водой у острова Бьяла: Off the port of Izlude, underwater near Byalan Island, lies Captain Drake's ship. For a hundred years it has sunk everything that sails past, and the captain has never died. In its hold is a cargo he swore never to give up.
Город каналов и Часовая башня: City of Canals and the Clock Tower
Альдебаран — северный город каналов, где: Al De Baran is the northern city of canals, where everything answers to the clock on the tower. This spring the clocks started running backwards, and the city can't remember yesterday. The tower archive holds the chronicle of Midgard — and it records who first opened the gates of Glast Heim.
Некогда гордое королевство рыцарей и соб: A once-proud kingdom of knights and its cathedral fell in a single night: the lord of the castle made a pact with darkness for power, and by morning no one was left alive. The knights became Raydrics, the cathedral a crypt, and the Dark Lord settled in the churchyard. The dead watch still changes by the book — it just forgot what it's guarding against.
Земля мёртвых за рекой Гьёлль: The Land of the Dead Beyond the Gyoll
Нифльхейм — земля, куда уходят все: тума: Niflheim is the land where everyone ends up: fogs, a village of the dead, the river of oblivion, the golden Gyoll Bridge and the citadel. Hel rules there, and there no one is hungry and no one hurries. After the Great War the gates between the living and the dead were closed — from the inside, so that only one who chose to stay could guard them.
Лес-лабиринт в двух часах от Пронтеры: The Labyrinth Forest, Two Hours from Prontera
Лес, в котором тропы меняются, пни повто: A forest where the paths shift, the stumps repeat and the hollows whisper bargains. Those who keep to the edge come home by lunch with firewood; those who go deeper keep coming out at the same clearing until they agree to a deal. Baphomet lives in that clearing. They say he keeps what opens the gates of Niflheim from this side: the consent of the living.
Королевство людей между горами Мьёльнир: The kingdom of humans between the Mjolnir Mountains and the sea. Its heart is Prontera with its cathedral and castle; to the west lies Geffen, city of mages; to the east, the port of Izlude; to the south, the Sograt Desert and Morroc; to the southeast, Payon in its pine forests; and in the north, Al De Baran. The guilds of swordsmen, archers, mages, thieves, acolytes and merchants welcome anyone ready to learn.
Мировое древо держит на корнях три мира:: The World Tree holds three worlds on its roots: Midgard of humans, Asgard of the gods and Niflheim of the dead. When the tree weakens, the barriers between worlds grow thin — and monsters grow bold even in peaceful meadows. Old-timers in taverns say it was like this before the Great War of the gods.
